plan.original_question: how should my personal lab can combine personal hybrid search with agent workflows ?
plan.research_objective: Identify and compare approaches for integrating hybrid search mechanisms (combining vector-based and keyword-based retrieval) with LLM-driven agent workflows in a personal AI lab setting.
sub_questions: What are the core components and design patterns of hybrid search systems?
How do existing agent workflow frameworks (e.g., AutoGPT, LangChain agents, BabyAGI) incorporate external retrieval?
What techniques exist for coupling hybrid search outputs with agent reasoning loops (e.g., retrieval-augmented generation, tool-use, memory augmentation)?
What evaluation metrics and benchmarks are used to assess the effectiveness of hybrid search‑agent integrations?
What practical considerations (compute, latency, data privacy, maintenance) arise when deploying such systems in a personal lab environment?
search_queries: tool use agents with hybrid retrieval
personal AI lab hybrid search agent implementation
expected_evidence: peer-reviewed papers on hybrid retrieval methods
articles describing agent frameworks with retrieval capabilities
benchmark datasets and evaluation studies for retrieval-augmented agents
open-source code repositories demonstrating hybrid search‑agent integration
tutorials or blog posts detailing deployment in small-scale settings
plan.research_strategy: 1. Define scope: focus on recent (last 3 years) literature on hybrid search and agent workflows. 2. Query arxiv and openalex using the prepared search queries, collect titles/abstracts. 3. Filter for relevance to hybrid search + agent integration. 4. Extract key architectures, coupling mechanisms, and evaluation results from selected papers. 5. Survey open-source implementations on platforms like GitHub to identify practical patterns. 6. Synthesize findings into a comparative table of approaches, highlighting strengths, weaknesses, and resource requirements. 7. Outline a step‑by‑step prototype plan for a personal lab, including data preparation, hybrid index building, agent tool integration, and evaluation protocol. 8. Document limitations and future work directions.

report.executive_summary: Hybrid retrieval integrates BM25 keyword-based and dense vector semantic retrieval, often combined via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) to merge results. [1][2] The local evidence base does not provide further details on integration with LLM-driven agent workflows, evaluation metrics, or practical deployment considerations for personal lab environments.

key_findings.statement: Hybrid retrieval systems combine BM25 keyword retrieval and dense vector semantic retrieval, with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) as a method to fuse results from multiple retrievers.
